title: One Square Mile
subject: Section 14 from altitude: two pivots, a row field, a farmstead and shelterbelt; a creek that ignores the grid and runs through the neck
treatment: Aerial plat. The four forms ARE fields; the 8x8 Opepen grid and the survey section grid are drawn as one. Iron-oxide ink plus earth-red wash made from soil gathered on the drawn land. 24x24 in image.
unique: The only piece where the whole system is visible at once; the key to the other 79. 40+ hours.

title: Breaking
subject: Spring: first plowing of the quarter; a single team mid-furrow
treatment: Plan view. Furrows follow each form's own geometry (rings in the eyes, rows in the mouth); unbroken sod outside as tick marks.
unique: The first marks ever made on this ground.

title: Stand
subject: Summer: the crop up, irrigation running, heat
treatment: Plan view. Dense stipple for canopy; pivot wheel tracks as darker rings; one wash pass of diluted red for heat.
unique: The only 1/4 with wash; the fullest the land gets.

title: Windrows
subject: Fall: cut, raked into windrows, baled; dust from the swather
treatment: Plan view. Long curving windrows inside forms; round bales as solid dots; dust plume dry-brushed.
unique: The land being taken back off itself; the forms written in bales.

title: After the Blow
subject: Winter: snow over everything; stubble along old furrows; one coyote crossed at night
treatment: Plan view, almost blank paper. The silhouette survives only as stubble dashes.
unique: The figure is nearly erased and still unmistakable.

title: Dwelling
subject: A board-and-batten claim house; we look at a wall
treatment: Elevation. The silhouette is the absence in the wall: openings through which the far horizon shows.
unique: Silhouette as void in a structure.

title: Well
subject: Windmill and stock tank
treatment: Elevation. The wheel is the right eye, drawn as an engineer would; everything else must be found on site, not forced.
unique: The only mechanical drawing in the set.

title: Fence
subject: Three-wire fence, cedar posts
treatment: Plan. The silhouette as a claim made in wire; a gate left open at the torso.
unique: Silhouette as boundary only — no fill, no subject inside.

title: Dugout
subject: The first dwelling: a room cut into a bank
treatment: Cross-section. Soil strata, roots and stones hatched horizontally; the forms are excavated voids; a ladder in the torso.
unique: The only underground view in the set.

title: Grave
subject: The homestead grave nobody lists among the improvements
treatment: Elevation/plan. A small iron fence encloses the torso as a mound; the rest of the figure in faint graphite only.
unique: The emotional turn of the set. Must be drawn from a real, respectfully chosen site.

title: The Pens
subject: Corrals at the home place: round pen, square pen, holding pen, chute
treatment: Plan. Rails define the figure; cattle crowd into the left eye's square corner — they always do.
unique: Animal behaviour proves the geometry.

title: Gather
subject: A herd bunched and drifting into the wind
treatment: Plan from height. ~900 animals construct the silhouette; strays and two riders outside.
unique: The subject builds the silhouette by sheer count.

title: The Chute
subject: A bull loaded in the bucking chute, seen from the catwalk
treatment: Close plan. Dense red crosshatch of the back and horns; the chute gate and boards hold the torso. From the artist's own PBR photography.
unique: The closest, heaviest view in the set; the artist's own photograph as source.

title: Round Pen, Morning
subject: A colt worked in the round pen; only its tracks are left
treatment: Plan. Thousands of hoofprint crescents wear the right eye into a ring; the rest of the figure is untouched dirt.
unique: Animal absent; animal everywhere.

title: Remuda
subject: Saddle horses bunched at the wrangle, from above
treatment: Plan. Packed horse backs outside; the silhouette is the open ground they leave.
unique: Negative-space silhouette made of bodies.

title: Calving
subject: A cow licking a newborn calf in late snow
treatment: Elevation, sporting illustration. The pair sits in the mouth; the figure's other forms are snow left blank.
unique: The only birth. Tenderness without sentiment.

title: Saddle Horse
subject: A horse tied to a rail, weight shifted, one hind foot cocked
treatment: Elevation. Full sporting-illustration finish; the rail and the barn's shadow carry the silhouette behind it.
unique: The set's single conventional 'portrait' — earned by being the best-drawn animal in it.

title: Coyote
subject: Tracks circling the pens at night
treatment: Plan. The pens of WO-10-01 redrawn in faint line; a single track line orbits them.
unique: Predator's view of the stock; rhymes with WO-10-01.

title: Brand Book
subject: A page from a county brand book with one registered mark
treatment: Facsimile-like ledger page, hand-lettered. The silhouette appears once, small, as a registered brand.
unique: The only place the 'brand' idea is allowed — as an archive, not a gimmick.

title: Bones
subject: A cow skull and vertebrae found in the pasture
treatment: Natural-history plate. Skull and bones laid out so their placement — not their shapes — makes the figure.
unique: The herd's end; bridge into Field Notes.

title: Prairie Sunflower
subject: Helianthus petiolaris, ditch on the north line
treatment: Engraving vignette whose boundary is the figure; disk is the right eye; petals break the edge.
unique: Phyllotaxis disk; the specimen refuses the boundary.

title: Nest
subject: Western meadowlark nest with three eggs, in the grass at a fence corner
treatment: Specimen in the right eye; the rest of the figure survives only as pencil construction.
unique: Silhouette as unfinished underdrawing.

title: Burrowing Owl
subject: Owl at the mouth of a prairie dog burrow
treatment: Ink portrait, life size, standing in the mouth; the burrow mound shadows the torso.
unique: The only creature looking back at the viewer.

title: Soapweed
subject: Yucca glauca in seed
treatment: Pen and dry brush; the spray of blades crosses all four forms; pods weight the eyes.
unique: Radiating line that cuts across the figure.

title: Buffalo Grass
subject: Bouteloua dactyloides, a single sod plug
treatment: Root mass drawn below ground in the mouth and torso; leaves above. Cross-section like WO-05-04.
unique: Underground specimen; rhymes with the Dugout.

title: Horned Lark
subject: A horned lark on bare ground in February
treatment: Tiny bird, enormous empty paper; the figure only in faint wind-scour marks.
unique: Smallest subject in the set.

title: Barn Swallow
subject: Swallows over the stock tank at evening
treatment: Gestural flight lines: each swallow's path a single stroke; the paths' density defines the forms.
unique: The silhouette drawn by motion paths.

title: Grasshopper Year
subject: Hundreds of grasshoppers on a fence post and wire
treatment: Specimen-plate rigor at swarm scale; insects cluster inside the figure.
unique: Plague as pattern.

title: Monarch
subject: Monarch on showy milkweed
treatment: Watercolor-and-ink natural-history plate; the only piece where red stands in for orange.
unique: Colour substitution made explicit.

title: Big Bluestem
subject: Andropogon gerardii, turkey-foot seed heads
treatment: Tall stems run full height, bottom to top; the figure appears where stems are drawn heavier.
unique: Silhouette by pressure only.

title: Pasqueflower
subject: Pulsatilla, first flower of spring, through old snow
treatment: Spare: one flower in the left eye's square corner, everything else blank.
unique: Single specimen placed in the figure's only right angle.

title: Prickly Pear
subject: Opuntia pads and fruit
treatment: Pads as overlapping ovals built into the forms; spines as stipple halos.
unique: Plant growth that happens to obey the geometry.

title: Barbed Wire
subject: Specimen card of three historical wire patterns
treatment: Plate laid out as a collector's specimen board; wire twists describe the four forms.
unique: A human artifact catalogued as natural history.

title: Evidence
subject: Things found along the line: a horseshoe nail, a .30-30 case, a button, a bottle neck
treatment: Each object drawn life size and placed in a form; museum-tag hand lettering.
unique: The traces of human lives — no person drawn.

title: Shed
subject: A bullsnake's shed skin across the gravel
treatment: One continuous scaled line traces the outline of all four forms.
unique: Silhouette drawn by a found line.

title: Primary
subject: A red-tailed hawk primary feather
treatment: Feather life size, vanes hatched vane-by-vane; the shaft cuts the figure diagonally; rest in pencil.
unique: The most finely worked single object.

title: Mud Daubers
subject: Mud-dauber nests under the eave of the claim house
treatment: Cells of the nests built up as the forms; drawn from WO-05-01's wall.
unique: Animal architecture; links Field Notes to Improvements.

title: Cottonwood
subject: Cottonwood leaf and seed fluff in June
treatment: Leaf in the mouth; seed fluff drifting across everything as broken line.
unique: The set's lightest, airiest marks.

title: Topsoil
subject: A soil core from the pivot, drawn with a hand lens
treatment: Abstract: grain-by-grain stipple in the forms; no recognisable object.
unique: Pure abstraction born from observation.

title: Seed Head, December
subject: The same sunflower as WO-20-01, dead and seed-robbed
treatment: Dry, broken disk in the right eye; stems bent; snow as blank paper.
unique: Closes the year opened by WO-20-01.
